title: Connections and driver catalog over BeepDM

commands.note: Sibling BeepDM/BeepDataSources projects emit their own warnings on a clean rebuild; none are in a Beep.OilandGas.Desktop path.

gates.DAT-01 AC-1 (driver list from loaded ass: pass — discovery loads drivers from the assembled folder and from a loaded assembly; deduped by PackageName
gates.DAT-01 AC-2 (test distinguishes bad host: pass — OgConnectionFailureClassifier maps to distinct codes (connection-database-missing, connection-driver-missing, connection-host-unreachable, connection-credentials-rejected, connection-failed); 10 message cases plus missing-driver/missing-file precedence are unit-tested, and the driver-missing and database-missing codes are proven over real BeepDM
gates.DAT-01 AC-3 (local file database created: pass — OgDriverDiscovery.SelectLocalDriver requires CreateLocal && !InMemory and has no silent fallback; a unit test proves a local in-memory cache listed first is not chosen, and the integration test asserts the selected driver advertises local creation and that EnsureLocalAsync reports which driver created the file
gates.DAT-01 AC-4 (deleting a connection in us: pass — RemoveAsync refuses with connection-in-use while the data source is open; proven by Deleting_a_connection_that_is_open_is_refused
gates.DAT-01 AC-5 (active connection survives: pass — SaveDataconnectionsValues + LoadDataConnectionsValues round-trips across a fresh runtime
gates.DAT-01 AC-6 (no credentials in logs, aud: pass by construction — this stage stores no credentials; ConnectionProperties is what BeepDM persists

claims: A local SQLite database is created through the catalog, not by a view.
The connection definition survives a process restart and is listed by a fresh runtime.
A fresh runtime reopens the same database and the data written before the restart is still readable.
An unknown connection is refused with a reference, never an exception.
A failed test names which of the four actionable outcomes it was: missing file, missing driver, unreachable host or rejected credentials.
The local database is created by a driver that advertises local creation and is not an in-memory cache; a connection whose type has no driver is refused rather than guessed.
Every catch in the new code reports through IFailureReporter (SourceGuardTests still passes).
limits: Only the SQLite provider was exercised; the host/credential classification is proven by representative messages, not by a live SQL Server or PostgreSQL.
A provider whose wording matches no hint lands in connection-failed; the classifier lists are the place to extend.
The integration test seeds its own table; the full PPDM schema is DAT-02.
The UI page was constructed by the smoke run, not driven by a user.
No credentials, no remote provider, no concurrency.
